definitions.gloss: to frolic together; to play-fight; to romp; to roughhouse
definitions.explanation: For two or more people or animals to play together in a physical, lighthearted way — wrestling, chasing, tumbling. Implies affection and playfulness. Commonly used for young animals, children, or couples.

examples.japanese: {子猫|こねこ}たち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧じゃれ{合|あ}って⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
⟦{兄弟|きょうだい}→兄弟：00964_kyoudai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧じゃれ{合|あ}って⟦いたら→いる：00495_iru⟧、⟦{本気|ほんき}→本気：03153_honki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{喧嘩|けんか}→喧嘩：02996_kenka⟧になった。
examples.english: The siblings were roughhousing, and it turned into a real fight.

examples.japanese: ⟦{公園|こうえん}→公園：00581_kouen⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{犬|いぬ}→犬：00632_inu⟧たち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{楽|たの}しそう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧じゃれ{合|あ}って⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦{姿|すがた}→姿：03363_sugata⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦こちら→こちら：00960_kochira⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{笑顔|えがお}→笑顔：01884_egao⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: Seeing dogs happily frolicking together in the park makes me smile too.

notes:
Godan verb (わ row): じゃれ{合|あ}う・じゃれ{合|あ}います
て-form: じゃれ{合|あ}って
た-form: じゃれ{合|あ}った

FORMS:
From ⟦じゃ→じゃ：03040_ja⟧れる (to play, to frolic) + ⟦{合|あ}う→合う：10466_au⟧ (reciprocal suffix indicating mutual action).

USAGE:
Very commonly used for animals, especially kittens, puppies, and other young animals. Also used for children and occasionally for couples being playfully physical. The ～⟦{合|あ}う→合う：10466_au⟧ suffix emphasizes the mutual, reciprocal nature of the play.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦じゃ→じゃ：03040_ja⟧れる: To play, to frolic — used for a single subject playing with something or someone, without the reciprocal nuance.
- ふざけ{合|あ}う: To joke around together — focuses more on verbal or silly behavior rather than physical play.
